title: Split lint by language and add incremental toolchain verifier
author: Priya Desai
description: Motivation: our monolithic lint runner has grown heavy (multi-language toolchain installs, slow cold starts) and is the largest contributor to presubmit setup time. This PR splits lint into language-aware runners and introduces an incremental toolchain verifier to dramatically reduce setup cost while preserving hermeticity and reproducibility. Goals: 1) Reduce presubmit walltime for common small changes by avoiding full toolchain installs; 2) Make CI more debuggable by isolating language-specific failures; 3) Keep a safe fallback to the legacy monolithic runner during rollout. What I changed (summary): - Introduced four lightweight lint runners: lint-python, lint-typescript, lint-go, lint-rust. Each runner uses a trimmed container image with only the language runtime, package manager, and cached toolchain artifacts. - Added ci/toolchain-manifests/* per-language manifests (pinned installers + checksums) and a new step: incremental-toolchain-verifier that verifies a workspace against the manifest and only fetches missing pieces. - Reworked .github/workflows/presubmit.yml to fan out lint jobs based on changed paths (path filters) and added a small orchestrator step to fall back to legacy-lint when multiple languages change in the same PR. - Added a local dev shim (scripts/ci/dev-lint-emulate.sh) so engineers can run the same verifier locally and reproduce CI behavior. - Improved caching: toolchain layer cache-key is now deterministic based on manifest hash + distro snapshot. Rollout plan: staged rollout by repo tag group; enable language-aware runs for high-volume repos first, enable fallback-window metric for 72 hours, then flip monolith off. Observability: new presubmit metrics (presubmit.setup_time_ms, presubmit.cache_hit_ratio) and alerts for >30% fallback rate. Backwards compatibility: default behavior remains unchanged until repo opt-in; the orchestrator emits a deprecation-warning event post-rollout to help teams migrate. Checklist: - [x] implement language-specific runner images - [x] add toolchain manifests and verifier - [x] update presubmit workflow with fan-out and fallback - [x] add local dev shim and docs - [x] metrics + alerts - [x] smoke rollout in infra/* repositories How this reduces cost/time: measured on the infra repo sample, median presubmit setup drops from ~95s to ~28s for small Python/Ts changes (cache hit path). For cross-language large changes the legacy fallback path keeps correctness. Risks and mitigations: - Risk: manifest drift causing unexpected CI failures. Mitigation: verifier fails clearly and suggests the exact manifest delta; automatic bot PRs to update manifests when onboarding new tool versions (future work). - Risk: flakier path detection. Mitigation: early rollout with high-verbosity logging and a quick revert plan. Related: ENG-2123 tracks the orchestrator feature; SUP-4521 is a customer incident that motivated faster presubmit feedback.

review_comments: Ethan Cole: Nice separation. Two asks: 1) can we keep a single cache key helper rather than duplicated logic across runners? 2) add a short-circuit if manifest hash matches workspace hash to reduce verifier overhead.
Priya Desai: Addressed — introduced ci/cache/key-helper.sh and added an early-exit in verifier when hashes match (second commit).
Marco Alvarez: Please add a note about how this affects release branches (we must not change presubmit on release/*). Added a guard to the workflow to ignore release branches.
Lina Zhou: Approve after CI passes and a short live rollout in infra/* (I ran a smoke test on infra/observability and results look good).
release_notes: Introduce language-specific lint runners and an incremental toolchain verifier to reduce presubmit setup time and improve debuggability. Opt-in rollout, no immediate breaking changes. See docs/ci/language-runners.md for migration steps.
